description: Use colors and shapes to make ideas clear. Learn how to help words stand out. Give readers more than one clue.

questionVariants: What is a color palette?
What do you choose when you plan a palette?
What does a palette hold for one design?
answerVariants: A small set of colors chosen for the page.
The group of colors picked for a design.
A planned group of colors to use together.

questionVariants: Where is the background in a design?
What part of a page is called the background?
Where does a background sit compared with words and pictures?
answerVariants: Behind the words, pictures, and other parts.
It is the area behind the other things.
At the back, under the other parts of the page.

questionVariants: Where are the foreground parts of a page?
What is in the foreground of a design?
Where do foreground objects appear?
answerVariants: In front of the area at the back.
On top of the background.
They sit in front of the background.

concepts.conceptName: Use an Accent in a Few Places
questionVariants: How should you use an accent color?
Where should the special accent color go?
How can an accent color keep its power to draw your eyes?
answerVariants: Use it on just a few key parts.
Save it for a small number of important spots.
Put it only where extra attention is needed.

questionVariants: What does emphasis mean?
What is the job of emphasis on a page?
What happens when a design gives one part emphasis?
answerVariants: One part draws more attention than the rest.
A key part stands out from the others.
One part is made easier to notice first.

questionVariants: What does contrast mean?
What makes contrast between two parts?
How would you explain contrast in a design?
answerVariants: A clear difference, such as light and dark.
A strong difference in things like size or lightness.
A difference that helps things stand apart.

concepts.conceptName: Choose Clear Text and Background Colors
questionVariants: Which text colors work well on a very light page?
What is a good text choice for a white background?
Pale words fade on a light page. What color choice can help?
answerVariants: Black or dark gray letters.
Dark letters, such as black or deep gray.
A very dark color for the words.

concepts.conceptName: Give More Than a Color Clue
questionVariants: A chart uses only red and green dots. What should you add?
How can a color chart help readers who cannot tell the colors apart?
How can colored status dots still make sense without their colors?
answerVariants: Add words, marks, or patterns that tell the meaning.
Use labels or symbols as a second clue.
Put a clear word or symbol beside each dot.

concepts.conceptName: Color Meaning Depends on People and Place
questionVariants: Does a color mean the same thing to everyone?
Will every group understand a color in the same way?
Can you assume one color always has one meaning?
answerVariants: No. People and places can give it different meanings.
No. Its meaning can change with the people or setting.
No. Different groups may understand it in different ways.

concepts.conceptName: A Form Such as a Circle or Box
questionVariants: What is a shape in a design?
What do circles, triangles, and rectangles have in common?
What kind of design part can have three sides or be round?
answerVariants: A form with its own outline.
A form with a clear edge or outline.
A form defined by its outer edge.

concepts.conceptName: Put Related Ideas in One Box
questionVariants: What can a box around a fact and its picture show?
How does one shape around related words and an icon help?
What does a shared box tell a reader about the things inside?
answerVariants: Those parts belong together.
The things inside form one group.
They are connected parts of one idea.

concepts.conceptName: Use a Line to Separate Parts
questionVariants: What job can a thin line do between two sections?
How can a line help divide a page?
Why might you put a line between different groups of facts?
answerVariants: It shows where one group ends and another starts.
It marks a break between groups.
It keeps separate parts clearly apart.

questionVariants: What job can an arrow do in a design?
How can an arrow help a viewer find the next step?
Why add an arrow to a path or set of steps?
answerVariants: It shows which way to go or look.
It points the viewer toward a place or next step.
It guides the eyes in a chosen direction.

concepts.conceptName: A Mark That Stands for an Idea
questionVariants: What is a symbol?
What does a symbol do in a design?
How can a small mark act as a symbol?
answerVariants: It stands for an idea, thing, or action.
It uses a visual mark to mean something.
It represents a meaning without a full sentence.

questionVariants: What is a pattern?
What makes a row of marks into a pattern?
How would you describe a visual pattern?
answerVariants: The same arrangement repeats.
A set of forms or marks repeats in order.
A visual arrangement is used again and again.

concepts.conceptName: Use Matching Styles for Equal Ideas
questionVariants: Why put three equal rules in matching boxes?
What do matching shapes tell us about a set of equal facts?
How do the same colors and boxes help related cards?
answerVariants: The matching look shows they belong to the same set.
The same style shows they are related and equal.
Their shared look connects them as a group.

questionVariants: How can you calm a page with many random colors and boxes?
Too many bright shapes fight for attention. What can help?
How can you fix a page full of unrelated visual styles?
answerVariants: Remove extra styles and repeat a smaller set.
Keep fewer styles and reuse them on purpose.
Cut extra colors and shapes, then reuse the ones you keep.

concepts.conceptName: Design So More People Can Use It
questionVariants: What does accessibility mean in a design?
What is the goal of accessibility?
How does accessibility help an audience?
answerVariants: More people, including people with disabilities, can use it.
It helps people with different needs get the information.
It makes information usable for people with a range of needs.

questionVariants: Why test a design in black and white?
What can a gray print test help you find out?
Why check a color chart on a printer that uses only black ink?
answerVariants: To see if the meaning stays clear without color.
To check that people can still read and understand it.
To make sure the message does not depend on colors.
